title: market-pain.json
description: The buyer's pain, in the buyer's words, with evidence a stranger can click. Written by gtme-market-pain; read by gtme-icp (who_feels + segments justify the tiers), gtme-offer (which problems earn components, via feature_ref and dream_outcome), gtme-write (statement + shape are the reader's own language) and gtme-measure (pain ids are the testable hypotheses). Facts about the SELLER belong in company.json; targeting decisions belong in icp.json. This schema is derived from the field spec in gtme-market-pain/SKILL.md - when the two disagree, the skill is the contract and this file is the bug.

sources_swept.description: Source CLASSES actually swept, not individual URLs - those live in provenance.md. A class listed here that produced no citation is a claim of work that left no trace.

pains.description: Ranked by how loudly the pain is felt, not by how well the seller solves it.

id.description: Permanent. messages.jsonl and measure.json tag against these, so renaming one silently breaks reply attribution.

statement.description: One sentence in BUYER voice that a practitioner would nod at. Seller-insight prose ('unmeasured loss is unpriced risk') is copy, not evidence, and fails the review question.

shape.description: The same pain at three rungs. gtme-write picks the rung by channel and persona.

personal.description: What the owner privately fears. MANDATORY - emotional-layer copy is written against this rung, and it is the hardest evidence class to find. If genuinely unavailable, the reason goes in decisions.md, not a placeholder here.

workflow.description: Step-level, named-tools depth: the queue tool they sit in, the step that stalls, the metric that punishes them, who they escalate to. The practitioner test lives here.

confidence.description: Strength of the PUBLIC evidence. A direct customer statement overrides this regardless.

type.description: felt = they already name it. latent = the hidden gap the seller reveals, which is where a wedge lives - but a latent pain with no revealing feature is a guess, so feature_ref cannot be null when type is latent.

felt_evidence.description: Why we believe it is FELT rather than merely true: someone paying, hiring, or complaining about it today. Required when type is felt.

segments.description: Read by gtme-icp: a tier's company_type list must be justifiable by the segments that actually feel the pain.

dream_outcome.description: Keyed by persona: what THAT role wants, in their language. Lives here only - gtme-offer selects from it and icp.json stays a clean filter.

oneOf.description: No capability kills this pain. Legal, and a finding: the pain is content-only or disqualifying, and decisions.md must say which.

feature_ref.description: The company.json feature or property id that kills this pain. Mapped pain -> feature, never feature -> pain. gtme-offer requires every solution to trace to a real capability; without this it re-derives the link by guessing. A feature no pain points at is a feature in search of a problem.

gap_math.description: A computable model, not a sentence. The reader does the arithmetic on their OWN numbers, which is why a prose figure is worth less: 'your 12 analysts x 30 cases/day' lands where an industry average does not.

observables.description: The inputs to the gap math that come from the prospect. `constants` in the same field already carried source and evidence_class while these were three bare words, and two of the three could not be obtained before contact at all. Unmarked, a writer either invents them or drops the math - and inventing a number in an email to a fraud team is this seller's worst failure mode.

findable.description: `public` means obtainable from outside before any contact. `must_ask` means it only exists inside the account, so copy must ask for it rather than assert it.

how.description: Required in spirit for `public`: where it is actually found.

constants.description: Conservative and cited. A dramatic number the reader can refute kills the whole map, so prefer the defensible bound.

evidence_class.description: How much weight the number can carry, travelling with it the way company.json's verification travels with a claim. primary = a regulator, federal series, association study or peer-reviewed paper. vendor_consensus = several vendors converge and NO neutral source exists; usable, but say so in copy. assumption = we picked it, and the citation only records where the guess came from. Bought by a real near-miss: two authoritative-sounding benchmarks in circulation for minutes-per-alert (one attributed to ACAMS, one to a named journal) both trace to a single vendor blog with no findable underlying document. An assumption that reaches copy wearing a citation is the failure this field prevents.

then.description: A felt pain carries >=2 independent citations: one quote is an anecdote, and the map's credibility is clickable evidence.
A latent pain with nothing revealing it is a guess, not a wedge.

tried_and_failed.description: What the buyer already bought and resented. Every row is an objection waiting in a first call.

complaints.description: Named-vendor gripes at verbatim grain. A category-level disappointment averages four products into one sentence and loses the specifics - gtme-write quotes these for displacement, gtme-offer answers them in the incomparability question.

verbatim.description: The complaint as the reviewer wrote it. Not your summary of it.

predicted_objections.description: Ranked per persona; gtme-write pre-handles the top one in copy.

answered_by.description: The offer element that handles this, as `<field>:<id>`. Null is a legitimate answer and means the objection is unhandled: gtme-write must not raise it and must not write copy that walks into it. Without this field the objections were researched, evidenced, and read by nothing.

awareness.description: Per segment, how aware the buyer already is - which selects the copy register gtme-write opens in. A bare label is an uncited assertion driving a real decision, so each carries its own evidence.

level.description: Schwartz's five. problem_aware needs the problem named; solution_aware is already comparing vendors and resents being taught what a false positive is.

default.description: The register to assume for a segment with no researched entry. Segments enter the ICP faster than awareness is researched, and a missing level makes the writer guess between two opposite emails.

level.description: Schwartz's five. problem_aware needs the problem named; solution_aware is already comparing vendors and resents being taught what a false positive is.

pain_keywords.description: DERIVED buyer search and complaint vocabulary. gtme-publish and gtme-signals read this.

market_pain_stats.description: Category-level numbers usable in copy, conservative figures preferred. Each carries the SCOPE it is true within, because a stat quoted outside its scope is how a defensible number becomes an indefensible one.

source.description: Who produced it. 'vendor-cluster consensus' is an honest answer; a laundered attribution is not.

market_verdict.description: The starving-crowd gate. do_not_run BLOCKS gtme-icp - a flawless ICP inside a dying vertical is still a dead campaign, and finding that out at the reply stage costs a full cycle.

note.description: One clause naming the binding constraint, when the four scores alone would mislead.

cites.description: Numbered references into this folder's provenance.md.
